one_month_reasoning: No Nutanix earnings fall in the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected around late November / early December 2026 (Q1 FY26 was reported in late November 2025; one aggregator estimates Dec 2). The quiet period starts around Oct 17. Events inside the window: the President/CCO Tarkan Maner leaves on Oct 2, but this was announced Sept 24 and is mostly priced in. September CPI comes in mid-October. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28, with Kalshi and Polymarket putting about 56% on a second hike, as of Sept 20; a hike would weigh on long-duration software but is close to priced. Peers also report in late October. The stock has rallied from $38 to $70 since March. Short-horizon momentum and post-beat drift (Q4 beat on Aug 26) lean slightly positive, while reversal after a near-doubling leans slightly negative, so I see no clear edge. The distribution is lognormal, centred at $70.9 (roughly flat), with a monthly sigma of 13% (47% annual vol / 3.5).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS of about $2.66 x 25x = $66.5) and EV/FCF (FY28 FCF of about $1.03B x 18x, plus about $1.0B net cash, over 292.7M diluted shares = $66.8). Rounded to $67.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (NTM at Oct-2027) non-GAAP EPS $2.66 x 25x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus $2.31 grown 15%: revenue growth in the low-to-mid teens (FY27 guide of 12%, FY29 target of mid-to-high teens) plus margin expansion toward mid/high-20s and continued buybacks ($483.5M in FY26).

Today's price is 30.6x FY27 consensus and about 26.6x my FY28 figure. I cut that to 25x because the Fed is hiking again (Sept 16 hike, about 56% odds of an October hike) with CPI at 3.4%. NTNX's own recent EV/FCF range of about 16-26x also points to a mid-20s P/E for a 12-15% grower.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $1.03B x 18x EV/FCF = EV $18.5B, plus net cash $1.01B = $19.55B equity, over 292.7M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 revenue of about $3.6B (FY27 guide midpoint $3.205B +12%) at about 28.5% FCF margin, the high-20s FY29 target. Cross-check: MarketScreener FY28 cash flow/share of $3.65 x ~285M shares is about $1.04B.
$777.3M cash + $1,584.2M ST investments - $1,348.7M convertible notes, at 7/31/2026

NTNX's normalized EV/FCF has run about 16-26x over FY24-FY26 (20.4x FY24, 26.4x FY25, 18.4x FY26), and today it is about 22x FY27 guidance. I take the lower-middle of that range: SBC is heavy and excluded from FCF, and rates are rising.

bear.story: This repeats the November 2025 pattern, when the stock went from $71 to $47 after a guidance cut: supply-chain/OEM constraints or memory-cost inflation push out revenue, growth slows to below 10%, the CCO's exit disrupts sales, and further Fed hikes or a 2027 recession (35% on Polymarket) compress the multiple to about 18x roughly $2.35 EPS.

base.story: Nutanix hits FY27 guidance of about 12% growth and a 24-25% margin, VMware migrations keep ARR growing in the mid-teens, and the multiple drifts down slightly as rates stay high. The price compounds with EPS to about 27x FY28 EPS of $2.66.

bull.story: VMware displacement accelerates (Gartner expects 70% of VMware customers to move half their workloads by 2028), the external-storage and AMD/NVIDIA AI deals add growth, guidance is raised toward the high-teens FY29 targets, and the stock re-rates to about 33x FY28 EPS of about $3.00.

thesis_break_reason: $46 is about 17x FY28 EPS, about 13x FY28 FCF ex-cash and below the post-cut trough of late 2025 ($47.80 at the end of November 2025). The stock has only traded there after a guidance cut or a major macro sell-off. A sustained move there would most likely mean FY27 guidance is broken (supply chain, sales execution after the CCO's exit, or VMware migrations stalling) rather than ordinary 47%-vol noise.

reasoning: Base rates first. NTNX's own 70 rolling 12-month returns (monthly closes, 2019-2026) have a median of +21% with an IQR of -12% to +62%, 5th/95th percentiles of -50% and +103%, and 64% positive. Realized vol is about 50% (47% over the last 24 months). That history is skewed upward by the 2023-24 re-rating from a cash-burning to an FCF-positive company, so I do not carry the +21% drift forward. The stock has had two sharp drawdowns on guidance cuts (Nov 2025: $71 to $48; Jan-Apr 2026 low of $34), and each time it recovered to the $70s within 6-9 months once beats resumed. The current setup is the post-recovery phase: Q4 FY26 beat (revenue $757M +16%, EPS $0.60 vs $0.49 expected), FY27 guide of 12% growth, 24-25% margin and $850-950M FCF, with targets raised to $79-90 (average $76.8, 15 analysts). Valuation: 30.6x FY27 EPS and about 22x FY27 FCF EV. My blended fair value of $67 is slightly below spot because the macro is now worse for multiples: the Fed hiked on Sept 16 and markets see more hikes, CPI is 3.4%, and Polymarket puts recession by end-2027 at 35% on thin volume of about $9.6k. Against that, the VMware migration tailwind is structural and well documented, and earnings growth of about 15% a year roughly offsets modest multiple compression. I centre the 12-month distribution with a median of about $69.5 (slightly below spot: fair value $67, analyst average $77, drift from EPS growth) and an effective log-sigma of about 0.40-0.43, slightly below the 47% realized vol because the business is now FCF-stable. I add a left-tail mixture component (20% weight, median $58, sigma 0.5) for the repeatedly observed guidance-cut drawdowns. Scenario mean of about $71.5 is consistent with that. Research was focused (about 12 queries); I relied on aggregator pages for consensus and multiples, and checked financials against the SEC 8-K.
